metadata.workstream: W-01 · Replace city and county proxies with trade-area figures
metadata.subjectGeography: Central Los Angeles (Exact Parcel / APN / Street Address Redacted — Internal Workspace Only)

indicators.indicator: Total Population — Latest State Official Estimate (Jan 1, 2026)
indicators.impact: CA DOF attributes LA County's 2025–2026 loss to Palisades/Eaton wildfire displacement, Inland Empire out-migration, and deportations. Contracting macro population caps organic QSR traffic growth unless local infill densifies the trade area.
indicators.sourceLabel: CA Dept. of Finance E-1 Report (May 2026)

indicators.indicator: Total Population — U.S. Census Bureau Estimates (V2025 vs. 2020 base)
indicators.impact: Census July 1, 2025 estimates and CA DOF January 1, 2026 estimates refer to different dates and methods. CA DOF cautions that they generally should not be directly compared; see Flagged for Review. Both county series are below their respective 2020 baselines, but do not imply parcel-level trends.
City of LA density is 3.4x the county average; high urban density underpins land scarcity for Central LA commercial corridors, though parcel-level tract density must be verified offline.
Regional income figures are not parcel trade-area data and do not establish site-level spending or sales.

indicators.indicator: Per Capita Income & Poverty Rate (2020–2024 ACS)
indicators.countyLA: $45,792 per capita (2020–2024 ACS); 13.3% poverty (latest QuickFacts value)
indicators.cityLA: $47,685 per capita (2020–2024 ACS); 16.5% poverty (latest QuickFacts value)
indicators.impact: Regional income and poverty context only; do not infer customer mix, spending power, or restaurant performance for the subject trade area.

indicators.indicator: Housing Tenure & Median Owner-Occupied Value (2020–2024 ACS 5-Year)
indicators.impact: Regional housing tenure and value are context only. Neither establishes the subject site’s trade area, rent burden, land value, or redevelopment feasibility.

indicators.indicator: MSA Nonfarm Payroll Employment (Sep 2026 Preliminary, NSA)
indicators.countyLA: LA-Long Beach-Anaheim MSA: 6,282,100 (+30,200 / +0.5% YoY; not stat. significant)
indicators.cityLA: City-level workplace mix spans Healthcare, Retail, Professional Services & Hospitality
indicators.impact: BLS reports +0.5% MSA over-the-year payroll change, not statistically significant at the stated confidence level. This regional measure is not a local tract or QSR sales forecast.

indicators.indicator: MSA Unemployment Rate (Sep 2026 Preliminary & 2021–2025 Annual Averages)
indicators.impact: The LA-Long Beach-Anaheim MSA unemployment series is a regional proxy, not an estimate for the subject tract or parcel.
indicators.sourceLabel: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Monthly Metro Release (Oct 2026)

indicators.countyLA: Index 360.965 (Oct 2026, +0.6% MoM); Sep 2026 12-mo change: +3.7% (Oct 12-mo blank in BLS)
indicators.cityLA: US Food Away From Home CPI-U: +3.5% YoY (May 2026) / +3.8% YoY (Mar 2026)
indicators.impact: Persistent ~3.5%–3.7% local inflation erodes flat or low-bump NNN leases while favoring uncapped CPI escalations. Flagged: BLS table shows '-' for Oct 2026 12-mo YoY.

indicators.indicator: California Fast Food Minimum Wage (AB 1228) & LA City General Minimum Wage
indicators.countyLA: CA Fast Food (AB 1228): $20.00/hr (eff. Apr 1, 2024); CA General: $16.90/hr (Jan 1, 2026)
indicators.cityLA: City of LA General Minimum Wage: $18.42/hr (eff. Jul 1, 2026, CPI-W indexed)
indicators.impact: The $20 fast-food floor applies to covered fast-food employers under AB 1228; the citywide minimum wage is jurisdiction-specific and not added to a higher applicable rate. Confirm site jurisdiction and applicable rules privately.
indicators.sourceLabel: CA DIR AB 1228 FAQ & LA Office of Wage Standards (2026)
indicators.sourceLabel2: City of Los Angeles 2026 official wage notice

indicators.indicator: LAUSD Enrollment, Graduation Rate & 10-Yr County K-12 Forecast

indicators.cityLA: LAUSD 2025–26 enrollment: 497,105 (16.4% English learners); 2024–25 graduation rate: 86.5%
indicators.impact: These districtwide metrics are not school assignments or parcel trade-area characteristics; use as regional context only.

indicators.cityLA: D Line Section 1 opened May 8, 2026; Sections 2 and 3 remain under construction; no exact completion date assumed.

indicators.indicator: LA City Community Plans, TOC Incentives & CA AB 2011 Commercial-to-Housing Law

indicators.impact: Zoning, TOC, plan designations, lot eligibility, and any redevelopment value require parcel-specific legal/planning review; no redevelopment uplift is assumed.

projectionFramework.metric: Official Agency Macro Baseline & Capital Markets
projectionFramework.baseProjection: CA DOF shows LA County -0.6% YoY & LA City -0.9% YoY population as of Jan 2026; BLS Sep 2026 MSA jobs +0.5% YoY; CA EDD projects +8.8% statewide job growth 2023–2033 led by Education & Health and Leisure/Hospitality; BLS Sep 2026 LA CPI-U +3.7% YoY; U.S. 10-Yr Treasury 4.91% (11/24/2026).
projectionFramework.upsideCase: Full D Line opening (Sections 2 & 3 forecast 2027) + 2028 Los Angeles Olympics visitor/infrastructure surge + lower Treasury yields + JACK brand stabilization strengthen buyer liquidity.
projectionFramework.downsideCase: Macro downturn lifts LA unemployment while AB 1228 ($20/hr) + persistent inflation compress franchisee margins, elevating 'JACK on Track' store-closure risk ahead of 2030.
projectionFramework.classification: Observed agency series + qualitative scenarios; not a property forecast
projectionFramework.sourceLabel: California EDD — statewide jobs report (one observed input)

projectionFramework.metric: Structural Demographic, Debt Maturity & Land Value Trajectory
projectionFramework.baseProjection: CA DOF projects slowing state growth (0.13%/yr avg) and -240,800 LA County public K-12 enrollment over 10 yrs; SCAG Connect SoCal 2024 projects gradual LA County employment expansion to 5.461M by 2050; JACK's Series 2026-1 ($500M, ARD May 2031) and Series 2022-1 A-2-II ($503M, ARD Feb 2032) debt maturities land inside this exact lease rollover window.
projectionFramework.upsideCase: Transit-corridor zoning (TOC Tiers 1–4 / AB 2011 / DTLA 2040) establishes an urban infill land floor supporting redevelopment sale or high-credit replacement QSR lease.
projectionFramework.downsideCase: Simultaneous arrival of lease expiry, JACK 2031–2032 securitized debt refinancing, California property insurance inflation, and shrinking family demographics creates severe re-leasing or valuation risk.
projectionFramework.classification: Observed agency / issuer inputs + qualitative scenarios; not a property forecast
projectionFramework.sourceLabel3: SEC — Jack in the Box Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q
